title: Wire the reader fit reference and margin to the Papers formulas
description:
## What to build

The fit-formula port (tuxbooks-koe.11) computes Papers-correct scales, but the reader still feeds page 1 as the fit reference and passes no margin. Wire the reader to use the document max page size and the Papers spacing so mixed-size documents fit the way Papers does, and update the E2E fitFactor helper to match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fit derives from the document max page size, not page 1.
- [ ] The Papers margin (2 * spacing) is applied.
- [ ] Mixed-size fixtures match the oracle behaviour.
- [ ] The E2E fitFactor helper reflects the change.

## Blocked by

- View geometry: fit formulas and integer page sizing (closed).
close_reason: Fit wired to documentMaxPageSize and PAPERS_VIEW_SPACING (2 * 12px); E2E helper updated. PR #128 (commit 40288c8), just check OK; E2E harness not run here.

comments.author: Tuomo Tuunanen
comments.text:
Done on branch feat/pdfium-fit-wiring, commit 40288c8, PR #128 (https://github.com/tuunanet/tuxbooks/pull/128). Not merged.

What changed:
- Fit reference: PdfReader.tsx uses documentMaxPageSize(sizes), memoized on sizes, instead of sizes[0].
- Margin: pdfLayout.ts exports PAPERS_VIEW_SPACING = 12 (the oracle spacing, priv->spacing in pps_view_init). computePdfScale already took a spacing argument, and usePdfScale.ts now passes PAPERS_VIEW_SPACING, so every fit reserves 2 * 12px. Presentation mode inherits the same margin. The four fit mode names are unchanged.
- E2E: fitFactor(page, referencePageWidth = 612) returns (clientWidth - 24) / referencePageWidth. The Odd Sizes layout spec passes 792 (its widest page) and measures every page before asserting the final geometry.

Evidence:
- Mixed-size effect: new PdfReader test "fits against the document's largest page, not page 1" shows page 1 alone fits at 2x, then measuring the 1224pt page drops the scale to 1 (page 1 width 612px, page 2 1224px, zoom 100).
- Oracle: pdfLayout.test.ts is unchanged and still passes 59 tests, asserting the three fit scales and whole-pixel page sizes against oracle/expected/geometry.json with documentMaxPageSize and spacing 12.
- Reader: pnpm --filter frontend exec vitest run PdfReader.test.tsx -> 73 passed. Seven margin/reference expectations were updated: fit width, window resize, the 4K byte budget, Ctrl+wheel-from-fit, and three presentation tests.
- Gate: just check -> OK; frontend 991 passed, rust green. Two rust tests flaked under parallel load during earlier runs and passed on retry; both are unrelated to this frontend change.
- E2E harness was NOT run in this environment; the helper and spec were updated as the ticket asks.

Blocker: none.

title: View geometry: smooth-zoom scale-and-swap
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-koe (spec: PDFium-WASM engine and Papers view geometry).

## What to build

During a scale change, keep the previous bitmap on screen under a transform
while the new-scale render runs, then swap atomically, so there is no blank
frame between the gesture and the sharp raster.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A zoom commit never shows a blank page; a drawable bitmap is present
      throughout.
- [ ] The new-scale bitmap replaces the scaled one on completion.
- [ ] Zoom stress stays within the render budgets and memory caps.

## Blocked by

- View geometry: focal-anchor zoom and scroll policies.
close_reason: Scale-and-swap and reader policy wiring landed in PR #127 (commit 33d3821); no-blank unit and reader tests pass, focal-anchor center policy asserted, just check green.

comments.author: Tuomo Tuunanen
comments.text:
Done on branch feat/pdfium-smooth-zoom, commit 33d3821, PR #127.

What landed: scale-and-swap in PdfPageCanvas. The canvas keeps the geometry of the last bitmap it presented (lastPresentedRef). On a scale change it paints that bitmap under a CSS transform sized to the new page box and sets data-pdf-render-quality="scaled"; the completed new-scale buffer replaces it in one atomic blit and clears the transform. PdfReader.applyZoom moves the pages that held pixels into a stalePages set instead of dropping them, canvasPages keeps them mounted, and renderPermittedPages admits at most MAX_CONCURRENT_RENDERS pages to a fresh raster through the new renderEnabled prop. A stale page outside the budget keeps its scaled bitmap and starts no engine request until promoted. The color variant, document switch, and presentation flip reset stalePages; an ordinary zoom does not. Bitmap cache untouched: swap keys off the canvas, not the cache.

Policy wiring: the wheel commit now calls adjustmentValueForPolicy("center", ...) in pdfLayout. It captures the old adjustment in document-local coordinates at commit and applies it once the layout scale lands (guarded on targetScale). This replaces the DOM-ratio fixup. The no-anchor re-layout fallback in reanchorByFraction uses keepPositionValue; keyboard/toolbar/fit keep the reading anchor per docs/PDF-VIEW.md. The reader publishes data-pdf-scroll-policy ("center" or "keep-position").

No-blank evidence: PdfPageCanvas.test.tsx scale-and-swap tests assert data-pdf-render-quality="scaled" with transform scale(2, 2) while drawImage still holds the first buffer, then "final" with transform cleared and canvas width 1224 after release; a display-only canvas (renderEnabled={false}) stays scaled and makes zero getPage calls across the settle window. PdfReader.test.tsx "keeps every rendered canvas drawable through a zoom commit" mounts three rendered pages, zooms, and asserts all three remain mounted and drawable with none blank, the page outside the render budget staying scaled.

Focal-anchor assertion: PdfReader.test.tsx "holds the focal anchor through the wheel commit via the center policy" asserts scrollTop/scrollLeft equal adjustmentValueForPolicy("center", ...) on both axes and that the reader reports data-pdf-scroll-policy="center".

Tests added and how they run:
- frontend/tests/PdfPageCanvas.test.tsx, describe "PdfPageCanvas scale-and-swap" (2 tests).
- frontend/tests/PdfReader.test.tsx, the no-blank reader test and the reworked focal-anchor test.
- Focused: pnpm --filter frontend exec vitest run PdfPageCanvas.test.tsx PdfReader.test.tsx (75 passed).
- Full gate: just check (OK; 985 frontend tests plus the Rust suite).

Budgets: stale canvases are filtered by the render window and the active-canvas byte budget before mounting, so the set cannot grow past the budgeted window. Stale buffers were already mounted before the zoom, so peak memory stays within the pre-zoom budget plus the in-flight new renders. Fresh rasters stay bounded at MAX_CONCURRENT_RENDERS.

Docs: docs/PDF-VIEW.md smooth-zoom section describes the mechanism and resolves the open item (keys off a per-canvas last-presented bitmap, not the cache); CONTEXT.md adds the term "Scale-and-swap".

No blockers.

title: Flip the default engine to PDFium and retire MuPDF
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-koe (spec: PDFium-WASM engine and Papers view geometry).

## What to build

Switch the default engine to the PDFium adapter and retire MuPDF. Delete the
guardrails (worker recycling, failure escapes, device-argument release, Smart
Dark heap signals, transformed-image cache), remove the dependency, the Vite
plugin, and the obsolete fixtures, delete the tests that pinned MuPDF defects
and drop the smart-colour E2E, rewrite the PDF layer doc, and set ADR 0002 to
accepted. The cleanup lands with the flip because the guardrails must not
outlive the engine that needs them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PDFium is the only engine; MuPDF is gone from dependencies and build
      config.
- [ ] Guardrail code and the tests that pinned its defects are deleted, each
      with a recorded reason.
- [ ] The PDF layer doc describes the new engine and no longer documents MuPDF
      workarounds.
- [ ] The full gate passes.

## Blocked by

- Region render at device resolution.
- Text layer geometry and selection.
- In-book search and outline.
- Dark colour scheme and theme mapping.
- Engine-seam import boundary.
- Focal-anchor zoom and scroll policies.
- Smooth-zoom scale-and-swap.
close_reason: PDFium is the only PDF engine. MuPDF adapter, worker, flag, dependency, Vite plugin, guardrail code, and defect-pinning tests deleted. docs/PDF.md and CONTEXT.md rewritten. just check passes. PR #130 open, not merged.

Flip landed. Branch feat/pdfium-retire-mupdf, commit e44e1b7, PR #130 (not merged): https://github.com/tuunanet/tuxbooks/pull/130

title: View geometry: fit formulas and integer page sizing
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-koe (spec: PDFium-WASM engine and Papers view geometry).

## What to build

Align the fit width, fit page, and automatic formulas with Papers, and round
scaled page sizes to whole pixels before scroll offsets are computed. Covered by
the oracle fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The three fit modes match the oracle within tolerance on every fixture.
- [ ] Page sizes round to whole pixels before scroll offsets are computed.
- [ ] A zoom sweep over a fixture shows no sub-pixel page-size jitter.

## Blocked by

- Fidelity oracle harness and fixture corpus.
close_reason: Fit formulas, automatic rule, and integer page sizing ported in PR #122 (commit 2fadc64), verified against oracle fixtures; just check green.

comments.author: Tuomo Tuunanen
comments.text:
Done on branch feat/pdfium-view-geometry-fit, commit 2fadc64, PR #122.

What landed: pdfLayout.ts ports Papers' fit arithmetic and integer page
sizing. Automatic fit follows zoom_for_size_automatic: fit width for a
portrait or square page, min(width, height) for a landscape page. The old
Okular aspect-ratio rule and AUTO_FIT_ASPECT_RATIO_RELATION are gone. The
fit functions take the Papers margin (2 * spacing). displayedSizes rounds
every dimension through scaledPixels ((int)(points * scale + 0.5),
pps-render-context.c:112) before layoutSlots derives tops, so scroll offsets
stay whole pixels. documentMaxPageSize gives the fit reference
(pps_document_get_max_page_size).

Oracle: frontend/tests/pdfLayout.test.ts reads the committed
oracle/expected/geometry.json and asserts the three fit scales on all seven
fixtures within 1e-8, PpsView's whole-pixel page sizes at fit width exactly,
and a 501-scale sweep with integer sizes and no sub-pixel jitter.

Evidence: computed fit scales match the oracle to 9 decimals on every
fixture (single-page 1.633986928/0.939393939/1.633986928; mixed-sizes
1.633986928/0.738095238/1.633986928; portrait
1.679893024/0.883725902/1.679893024; landscape 1.187803632 on all three;
thousand-pages 1.633986928/0.883725902/1.633986928; scan and vector-heavy
as single-page). mixed-sizes page 4 raw 685.503268x972.673203 rounds to
686x973, matching the oracle.

Verification: pnpm --filter frontend exec vitest run pdfLayout.test.ts (59
passed) and just check (OK). 946 frontend tests still pass.

Limits: the reader still feeds page 1 as the fit reference and reserves no
margin (spacing defaults to 0), so this ticket changes the formulas, the
automatic rule, and integer sizing, not the reader's target. Wiring
documentMaxPageSize and the Papers spacing into PdfReader changes
mixed-document fit and the E2E fitFactor helper, so it stays a follow-up. No
blockers.

title: View geometry: focal-anchor zoom and scroll policies
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-koe (spec: PDFium-WASM engine and Papers view geometry).

## What to build

Pointer-anchored focal zoom and the two scroll policies, so a wheel or pinch
zoom holds the document point under the pointer, while keyboard and toolbar zoom
hold the reading anchor.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The point under the pointer stays fixed across a zoom on every fixture.
- [ ] Re-layout preserves the relative position; explicit zoom centres on the
      focal anchor.
- [ ] The oracle confirms the adjustment transform within tolerance.

## Blocked by

- View geometry: fit formulas and integer page sizing.
close_reason: Focal-anchor transform and both scroll policies ported in PR #125 (commit 8221eb9), verified against oracle zoom_script on all seven fixtures; just check green.

comments.author: Tuomo Tuunanen
comments.text:
Done on branch feat/pdfium-focal-zoom, commit 8221eb9, PR #125.

What landed: pdfLayout.ts ports pps_view_update_adjustment_value (pps-view.c:564). centerValue is the focal-anchor transform (SCROLL_TO_CENTER): factor = (value + zoom_center) / upper, new_value = CLAMP(new_upper * factor - zoom_center, 0, new_upper - page_size), negative centre = viewport middle. keepPositionValue is the re-layout policy (SCROLL_TO_KEEP_POSITION): the old value/upper fraction reapplied to the new content. adjustmentUpper is Papers' MAX(viewport, content), adjustmentValueForPolicy selects the branch. viewportPointToDocumentPoint, anchorAtOffset, and offsetForAnchor map offsets to page points so the oracle's center_anchor compares directly. usePdfScrollTracking now captures the reading anchor through anchorAtOffset and exposes anchorAtViewportOffset, the pointer-capture helper a wheel or pinch zoom uses. Keyboard and toolbar zoom keep the reading anchor; the reader's existing cursor fixup is unchanged, so the ticket is a geometry port in the .11 sense.

Oracle: frontend/tests/pdfScrollPolicy.test.ts reads oracle/expected/geometry.json and replays every zoom step on all seven fixtures. The adjustment value matches to 1e-8 on both axes; the derived page point equals center_anchor and its drift equals anchor_error (under 1 point); an off-centre pointer at 30% of the viewport stays under 1.5 points. Policy tests cover keep-position vs center, including top-of-document: keep-position 0, center 75.459787557.

Evidence: focused pnpm --filter frontend exec vitest run pdfScrollPolicy.test.ts pdfScrollTracking.test.ts (21 passed); just check (OK), 968 frontend tests plus the Rust suite.

Limits: the geometry is not wired into PdfReader's wheel commit yet. The reader still uses its own DOM-ratio fixup, which already holds the cursor point (PdfReader.test.tsx "keeps the point under the cursor fixed when the wheel gesture commits"). Adopting centerValue/keepPositionValue in the reader is follow-up shared with .13 and .16. No blockers. Closing.

title: Enforce the engine-seam import boundary
description:
## Parent

title: Engine adapter: dark colour scheme and theme mapping
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-koe (spec: PDFium-WASM engine and Papers view geometry).

## What to build

Dark rendering through PDFium's category colour scheme, mapped from the existing
palette, plus the CSS filter for scans. Smart Dark object recoloring and
scanned-image classification are dropped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dark and paper modes render text and vector content in the theme palette
      with photographs intact.
- [ ] The four colour modes keep their stored names and behaviour.
- [ ] The engine adapter holds no object-recolor device.

## Blocked by

- Engine adapter: open, page sizes, whole-page raster, range-backed open.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #129: dark mode via PDFium's category colour scheme mapped from the reader palette, paper via the existing CSS tint, with a real-WASM dark test and an adapter request test; MuPDF Smart Dark untouched

comments.author: Tuomo Tuunanen
comments.text:
Implemented in PR #129 on feat/pdfium-dark-colorscheme, commit b8600f2.

How the colour scheme is applied: the adapter converts the seam's dark
SmartPalette to PDFium's FPDF_COLORSCHEME, and the worker renders through
FPDF_RenderPageBitmapWithColorScheme_Start with a real IFSDK_PAUSE. A null
pause returns FPDF_RENDER_FAILED, so the worker allocates a version-1 pause
whose NeedToPauseNow returns 0 and drives FPDF_RenderPage_Continue until the
status is DONE. The bitmap is pre-filled with the scheme's path fill, so an
unpainted PDF page becomes the dark page colour. FPDF_CONVERT_FILL_TO_STROKE
strokes path fills with the light colour so adjacent fills stay visible.

The palette maps as: path fill is the palette background, path stroke and text
fill are the palette text, text stroke is the palette background, all 32-bit
0xAARRGGBB. For the dark preset that is path fill 0xFF101013, path stroke and
text fill 0xFFE4E4E7, text stroke 0xFF101013.

Photos and scans: PDFium translates only path and text categories, so images
draw unchanged and keep their pixels. Paper, invert, and contrast are
untouched (CSS multiply tint and CSS filters), so a scan can use Invert or
High contrast. Automatic scan classification stays dropped, per ADR 0002.

Region dark renders use the same progressive entry point with the start/size
box offset by the clip, since the colour-scheme API has no matrix variant. The
real-WASM test pins region alignment against the whole-page crop.

Tests:
- pnpm --filter frontend exec vitest run pdfiumEngine.node -> 11 passed, including
  the dark page (16,16,19), light title text, image pixels equal to the plain
  raster, and region alignment.
- pnpm --filter frontend exec vitest run pdfiumEngineAdapter smartColors -> 36
  passed, including the render request carrying the colour scheme.
- pnpm --filter frontend test:ci -> 68 files, 997 tests passed.
- just check -> check: OK.

Files: frontend/src/lib/pdf/{smartColors,pdfiumCore,pdfiumWorker,pdfiumEngine}.ts
and their tests. MuPDF Smart Dark (the smartColors object path, mupdfWorker.ts,
theme.ts) is unchanged; the MuPDF cleanup stays in .14.

title: Engine adapter: text layer geometry and selection
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-koe (spec: PDFium-WASM engine and Papers view geometry).

## What to build

Text extraction and per-character geometry through PDFium, feeding the existing
text layer, selection, and highlight overlay.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The text layer renders transparent selectable spans over a canvas.
- [ ] Selection produces normalized page-space rects the backend accepts.
- [ ] Existing highlights align at every zoom.
- [ ] Pages with no usable text degrade to no text layer without error.

## Blocked by

- Engine adapter: open, page sizes, whole-page raster, range-backed open.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #124: PDFium getTextLines for the text layer and selection; geometry within a few points of MuPDF; empty pages degrade to no layer; MuPDF stays default

comments.author: Tuomo Tuunanen
comments.text:
Implemented in PR #124 on feat/pdfium-text-layer, commit da984cd.

What the adapter covers: getTextLines for the PDFium engine, feeding the existing text layer, selection, and highlight overlay. MuPDF stays the default; PDFium text is opt-in with the same flag.

Extraction and geometry: pdfiumCore.ts textLines walks FPDFText_CountChars, FPDFText_GetUnicode, FPDFText_GetLooseCharBox, FPDFText_GetCharOrigin, and FPDFText_GetFontSize, groups characters by baseline, and returns the seam's EngineTextLine[] in page units with a top-left origin. Wide horizontal gaps become spaces when the content stream does not encode one. A page with no text returns [] and mounts no layer. pdfiumWorker.ts adds the text request. pdfiumEngine.ts requests it and caches the promise per page.

Fidelity: for tests/fixtures/books/minimal.pdf page 1, MuPDF structured text gives x=72, y=229, w=397, h=54, size=40. PDFium loose boxes give x=72, y=234.2, w=397.9, h=46.8, size=40, within a few points, and keep the font size.

Tests:
- pnpm --filter frontend exec vitest run pdfiumEngine passes 11 tests.
- frontend/tests/pdfiumEngine.node.test.ts drives real PDFium-WASM in Node and checks the two known lines and page-unit geometry.
- frontend/tests/pdfiumEngineAdapter.test.ts checks the text request reaches the worker, the per-page cache, renderPdfTextLayer span shaping at scale 2, and the empty-page degradation.
- just check passes.

title: Engine adapter: open, page sizes, whole-page raster, range-backed open
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-koe (spec: PDFium-WASM engine and Papers view geometry).

## What to build

A PDFium engine adapter that implements the `PdfDocument` and `PdfPage` seam
behind a feature flag: open, page sizes, whole-page raster, and range-backed
access. MuPDF stays the default until the flip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A book opens through the new adapter with the flag on and whole pages
      render.
- [ ] Range-backed open keeps the read-ahead cache and never reads the whole
      file.
- [ ] Page geometry matches the document.
- [ ] The flag off leaves current behaviour unchanged.

## Blocked by

- Engine decision (accept or reopen ADR 0002).

comments.author: Tuomo Tuunanen
comments.text:
Implemented in PR #120 on feat/pdfium-engine-adapter, commit 66a50a2.

What the adapter covers: open from bytes and range-backed open, page count, page sizes, and whole-page raster with the transform ratio. Region, text, outline, search, and the dark colour scheme stay reserved for .6 to .9. Region requests fail with a clear error and text and outline return empty, so the reader still opens and renders whole pages.

Flag: MuPDF stays the default. PDFium is opt-in with VITE_PDF_ENGINE=pdfium at build time, or localStorage["tuxbooks.pdfEngine"]="pdfium" at runtime. pdfEngine.ts dispatches open, prewarm, and worker URL selection. No reader component changed.

Range-backed open: FPDF_LoadCustomDocument with an FPDF_FILEACCESS whose m_GetBlock writes into the WASM heap, backed by a 1 MiB read-ahead chunk cache over tuxbooks://book/<id>. A small read never transfers the whole file.

Package: @embedpdf/pdfium@2.15.0, MIT. pdfiumCore.ts is the only runtime module that imports it.

Tests: pnpm --filter frontend test:ci passes 64 files and 938 tests. New: pdfEngineFlag.test.ts, pdfRangeSource.test.ts covering chunk reuse, the LRU bound, and an 8 MiB source that never reads whole, pdfiumEngineAdapter.test.ts in jsdom against a fake worker, and pdfiumEngine.node.test.ts driving real WASM: 3 pages, 612x792, non-white raster, range-backed open. just check passes. pnpm --filter frontend build emits pdfiumWorker and pdfium.wasm, the entry chunk grows 8.7 KB and stays free of PDFium glue.

Known limits: region render errors under the flag until .6, and dark mode renders without recolouring until .9. The browser WASM does not load under vitest jsdom, so the WASM assertion runs in a Node-environment test.

title: Engine adapter: region render at device resolution
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-koe (spec: PDFium-WASM engine and Papers view geometry).

## What to build

Region rendering on the adapter through `FPDF_RenderPageBitmapWithMatrix`, so
deep zoom rasterizes only the visible page region at device resolution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clipped render produces a region-sized bitmap positioned correctly in
      its page slot.
- [ ] Deep-zoom sharpness matches the current region-render behaviour.
- [ ] Region renders respect the pixel and byte budgets.

## Blocked by

- Engine adapter: open, page sizes, whole-page raster, range-backed open.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #121: PDFium region render at device resolution via FPDF_RenderPageBitmapWithMatrix; MuPDF stays default

comments.author: Tuomo Tuunanen
comments.text:
Implemented in PR #121 on feat/pdfium-region-render, commit 68b7bff.

What region render does: the adapter converts the CSS-pixel region into page units (pageSize.width / viewport.width), sizes the buffer to region.width x ratio by region.height x ratio, and sends { page, width, height, clip } to the worker. pdfiumCore.ts calls FPDF_RenderPageBitmapWithMatrix with FS_MATRIX [scaleX, 0, 0, scaleY, -left*scaleX, -top*scaleY] and FS_RECTF clip [0, 0, width, height] in device coords. The matrix scales page units to the region-sized bitmap and moves the region origin to 0,0, so the bitmap matches the same crop of a whole-page raster. PdfPageCanvas already absolutely positions the region-sized canvas in the page slot and carries data-pdf-render-region. The temporary koe.6 rejection is removed.

Budgets: the reader sizes region buffers with regionRenderRatio (PERF-17), which clamps to the 2^25-pixel hard cap and the 8192-pixel side cap, so no page-sized buffer is allocated at deep zoom.

Tests, pnpm --filter frontend exec vitest run tests/pdfiumEngine.node.test.ts tests/pdfiumEngineAdapter.test.ts: 2 files, 8 tests pass. Node WASM test renders clip [72, 243, 378, 40] on page 1 and matches it against the same crop of a 1:1 whole-page raster (under 2 percent of pixels differ by more than 8 per channel), checks a blank band at y=520 is pure white, and pins the deep-zoom buffer under MAX_RENDER_PIXELS_HARD. jsdom adapter test asserts the worker request { page: 1, width: 60, height: 80, clip: [20, 40, 60, 80] }. just check reports check: OK.

Files touched: frontend/src/lib/pdf/pdfiumCore.ts, pdfiumEngine.ts, pdfiumWorker.ts, and their two tests. pdfLayout.ts, the scale hook, and pdfRenderPolicy.ts are unchanged. MuPDF stays the default.

Done on branch feat/pdfium-oracle-harness, commit a853a45, PR #119.

comments.author: Tuomo Tuunanen
comments.text:
Phase 0 spike complete. Verdict: PASS. Prototype branch: prototype/pdfium-wasm-spike, worktree .worktrees/pdfium-spike, commit 14aeb25. Never merged.

PACKAGE: @embedpdf/pdfium@2.15.0 (MIT). Chosen over @hyzyla/pdfium (higher-level render wrapper, not the raw C surface the plan targets), pdfium-wasm (2023) and pdfium.js (0.2.1-rc, 2024) (stale). It exposes the raw FPDF_* API, and 2.15.0 is the newest release older than the repo's 30-day minimumReleaseAge (2.15.1 is 4 days old).

KILL CRITERIA
1. Rasterize in the renderer worker: PASS. Real classic Web Worker under Chromium 153 (the shape Emscripten's browser build needs), every FPDF call and range read inside it.
2. Byte budget: PASS. WASM 4,633,788 B raw / 1,649,352 B brotli; worker glue 287,276 B / 41,858 B. MuPDF 1.28.1 is 10,409,826 B raw / 3,622,011 B brotli plus 132,111 B / 26,097 B glue. PDFium total is 47% of MuPDF raw, 46% brotli. ADR's 6-11 MB estimate was pessimistic.
3. Range-backed open: PASS. FPDF_LoadCustomDocument + FPDF_FILEACCESS with sync-XHR m_GetBlock. On ai-engineering.pdf (31.29 MB, 991 pages): 222 range reads, 2,036,782 B (6.5%), open 120.8 ms. GeoTopo.pdf (5.32 MB, 117 pp): 189 reads, 687,386 B (13%), open 64.4 ms. Whole file never crossed. A 48 KB fixture reads whole (< read-ahead); expected. Every open touches EOF for the xref trailer.
4. Performance caps: PARTIAL PASS, risk named. Native whole-page raster p95 2.9-28.8 ms. Reference dpr-1 region (3840x2160) 1.5-71.9 ms. Reference dpr-2 region (7680x4320, the PERF-1 max) 29.8-225.7 ms; image-heavy pages exceed PERF-2's 100 ms. The documented MuPDF baseline is p50 147.5 / p95 176.5 ms (docs/PERFORMANCE.md PERF-2) and does not meet 100 ms either, so PDFium is comparable to or better than today. Region render is 7x faster than whole page (GeoTopo 8.7 ms vs 63.2 ms; 33.2 MB vs 83.4 MB), so PERF-17 holds. Recommend re-baselining PERF-2, not reopening the engine. First paint 179.8-225.9 ms, of which 25-29 ms is WASM init (removed by prewarm) and 47-121 ms the open.
5. Capability floor: PASS. Text (LoadPage/CountChars/GetText plus per-char box/origin/rect/matrix calls), outline (Bookmark_GetFirstChild/NextSibling/Title, GetDest + Dest_GetDestPageIndex), search (FindStart/FindNext/GetSchCount; matched 9/3/3), and FPDF_COLORSCHEME (recolor verified, 3552/6478/1742 non-white px) all present. No required API missing.

NAMED INTEGRATION DETAIL: the only color-scheme entry point is the progressive FPDF_RenderPageBitmapWithColorScheme_Start. It needs a valid IFSDK_PAUSE (version 1, NeedToPauseNow); a null pause returns status 3 (FPDF_RENDER_FAILED) and draws nothing. There is no color-scheme variant of FPDF_RenderPageBitmap or FPDF_RenderPageBitmapWithMatrix, so dark region rendering must use the progressive path (FPDF_RenderPage_Continue, FPDF_RenderPage_FPDF_RenderPage_Close). Status enum (PDFium fpdf_progressive.h): 0 ready, 1 to-be-continued, 2 done, 3 failed.

ARTIFACTS: .worktrees/pdfium-spike on prototype/pdfium-wasm-spike; reports/{geopoto,ai-engineering,pdflatex-outline}.json and prototype/pdfium-spike/README.md. Reproduce with: cd prototype/pdfium-spike && npm install && node runner/run-spike.mjs.

ADR 0002 NOT edited here: it lives on the unmerged docs/pdfium-renderer-plan branch (PR #118), outside this worktree, and ticket tuxbooks-koe.4 owns the accept/reopen decision. My recommendation to .4 is accept. No blocker.

title: Spec: PDFium-WASM engine and Papers view geometry for the PDF reader
description:
# Spec: PDFium-WASM engine and Papers view geometry for the PDF reader

## Problem Statement

Reading a PDF in TuxBooks is unreliable and expensive to maintain. The MuPDF
engine corrupts its own internal state on some pages, so the reader carries
workarounds (worker recycling, failure escapes, per-argument manual memory
release) that add hundreds of lines and tests which exist only to contain those
defects. Dark mode is implemented as an object-level recolor device, which is
where the corruption lives. The zoom and scroll feel is worse than GNOME
Papers. The app also ships an AGPL-3.0 dependency inside a GPL-3.0 project.

## Solution

Move PDF rendering to PDFium compiled to WebAssembly, and reproduce GNOME
Papers' zoom and layout behaviour on top of the reader's existing architecture.
The engine seam stays. The reader keeps its virtualization, render policy,
caches, text layer, search, outline, and progress. The MuPDF guardrails are
deleted as each capability moves. Dark mode falls back to a category-level
color scheme.

## User Stories

1. As a reader, I want PDF pages that crash the current engine to rasterize
   correctly, so that I can read the whole book.
2. As a reader, I want one page's failure to show a retry on that page and
   never break the document.
3. As a reader, I want to open a large PDF without waiting for the whole file
   to transfer, so that the first page appears quickly.
4. As a reader, I want the first page to appear within the current first-paint
   budget.
5. As a reader, I want to zoom with the mouse wheel and pinch and have the point
   under my cursor stay fixed, so that zooming feels controlled.
6. As a reader, I want fit width, fit page, and automatic fit to match Papers'
   arithmetic, so that pages fill the viewport the same way.
7. As a reader, I want page edges to stay crisp during zoom, with no shimmer
   from sub-pixel sizing.
8. As a reader, I want the page to stay readable during a zoom, showing the
   previous rendering scaled until the sharp one arrives, so that there is no
   blank frame.
9. As a reader, I want zoom stepping to keep the existing preset ladder.
10. As a reader, I want my reading position preserved through a window resize
    and restored exactly on reopen.
11. As a reader, I want presentation mode to keep working with the new engine.
12. As a reader, I want to select text and create highlights with the same
    geometry as before.
13. As a reader, I want in-book search to return matches with the same
    behaviour.
14. As a reader, I want the outline to resolve to the same page locators.
15. As a reader, I want thumbnails to render within the same budgets.
16. As a reader, I want dark mode to recolor text and vector content and keep
    photographs intact, accepting that the recoloring is coarser than before.
17. As a reader, I want light, paper, dark, and invert modes to keep their
    current names and behaviour.
18. As a reader, I want the reader to fall back to the previous engine if the
    new one fails to load.
19. As a maintainer, I want the engine to be swappable behind one seam, so that
    a future engine change touches one module.
20. As a maintainer, I want no reader component to import the engine package
    directly, enforced by a lint rule.
21. As a maintainer, I want the MuPDF guardrail code deleted when its capability
    moves, so that dead workarounds do not accumulate.
22. As a maintainer, I want tests that pin MuPDF defects deleted, and tests that
    pin reader contracts kept and repointed at a fake engine.
23. As a maintainer, I want the reader contracts documented with the new
    engine's behaviour.
24. As a maintainer, I want a native Papers harness that produces reference
    geometry for fixtures, so that fidelity is testable.
25. As a maintainer, I want the reimplemented geometry to match the harness
    within tolerance on the fixture corpus.
26. As a maintainer, I want the WASM bundle to stay in the same size range as
    today's.
27. As a maintainer, I want no AGPL-only dependency in the shipped app.
28. As a maintainer, I want import-time cover rendering to keep using native
    PDFium.
29. As a maintainer, I want the cleanup recorded in buckets so tickets can order
    it.
30. As a maintainer, I want the ADRs and the CONTEXT glossary to describe the
    new engine and view model.
31. As a reader, I want opening, closing, and switching books to free all engine
    resources.
32. As a reader, I want a stalled page render to be reported instead of freezing
    the UI.
33. As a reader, I want Ctrl+wheel zoom, keyboard zoom, and toolbar zoom to all
    produce sensible anchored results.
34. As a reader, I want the page indicator and navigation to stay in sync with
    scrolling.
35. As a QA engineer, I want E2E coverage for the reader and zoom stress to run
    on the new engine.

## Implementation Decisions

- Engine: PDFium-WASM behind the existing engine seam. The `PdfDocument` and
  `PdfPage` interfaces stay. `PdfPage.render` keeps whole-page, region, and
  transform options. `smartColors` becomes a color-scheme input rather than an
  object-recolor device.
- Range-backed open: `FPDF_LoadCustomDocument` with `FPDF_FILEACCESS`, keeping
  the bounded read-ahead cache.
- Region render: `FPDF_RenderPageBitmapWithMatrix` with the region clip.
- Text layer: PDFium text-page APIs for text and per-character geometry. Keep
  the current text-layer CSS contract.
- Search: PDFium find APIs. Keep the pure assembly helpers.
- Outline: PDFium bookmark APIs. Keep the normalization module.
- Dark mode: `FPDF_COLORSCHEME` plus the existing CSS filter path. Drop
  scanned-image classification for the first version.
- Worker model: keep one worker per document and cancellation. Remove worker
  recycling, the failure escape, the device-argument release ritual, and the
  Smart Dark specific heap signals. Keep generic stall reporting.
- View geometry: pure TypeScript. Fit formulas, integer page sizing, the
  focal-anchor transform, and the two scroll policies live in the layout module
  and the scale and scroll hooks. The smooth-zoom policy lives in the page
  canvas: while a new-scale render is pending, keep the previous bitmap under a
  transform and swap on completion.
- Fidelity oracle: a native Linux harness driving Papers' `PpsView`, emitting
  page extents, scroll values, and anchor points for a fixture corpus. Fixtures:
  single page, mixed page sizes, portrait and landscape, a 1000-page document, a
  scan, and a vector-heavy page.
- Cleanup buckets: (A) MuPDF-defect guardrails, delete with the capability;
  (B) MuPDF-style capability, replace behind the seam then delete; (C)
  engine-agnostic architecture, keep. Each ticket carries its bucket.
- Import rule: only the engine adapter may import the engine package.
- Contracts to update: `docs/PDF.md`, `docs/PDF-VIEW.md`, ADRs 0002 and 0003,
  `CONTEXT.md`.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests assert external behaviour, not engine internals. Reader-contract
  tests run against the fake `PdfDocument`, so they survive the swap.
- View geometry tests are pure and need no browser or engine. They run against
  oracle fixtures, asserting pixel-rounded extents exactly and float scales
  within epsilon, plus focal-anchor stability and the no-blank-frame invariant.
- Engine-adapter tests are integration-level and confirm the capability floor:
  range open, whole-page render, region render, text extraction, outline,
  search, and color scheme.
- Prior art: `pdfLayout.test.ts`, `pdfRenderPolicy.test.ts`,
  `pdfBitmapCache.test.ts`, `PdfReader.test.tsx`, `PdfPageCanvas.test.tsx`, and
  the fake engine in `tests/mocks/pdfEngine.ts`.
- Delete `pdfWorkerRecycle.test.ts`, `transformedImageCache.test.ts`, and most
  of `smartColors.test.ts` when their code goes. Drop `pdf-smart-color.e2e.ts`.
  Keep `pdf-reader.e2e.ts` and `pdf-zoom-stress.e2e.ts` and run them on the new
  engine.

## Out of Scope

- Dual-page and non-continuous layout modes.
- Scanned-image classification for dark mode.
- Kinetic scroll and the touch gesture model.
- EPUB reader changes.
- Native PDFium cover rendering changes.
- Windows and macOS packaging.

## Further Notes

- ADR 0002 is proposed until the Phase 0 spike passes. If the spike trips a kill
  criterion, the engine reopens to Poppler-WASM.
- The spike is a timeboxed prototype whose deliverable is a decision.
- The oracle harness is test-only and never ships.
- `tuxbooks/papers` is a reference-only submodule.
close_reason: Complete: PDFium engine shipped and MuPDF retired (PRs #118-#132); follow-ups filed as tuxbooks-koe.18 through .20

comments.author: Tuomo Tuunanen
comments.text: Epic complete. PDFium-WASM is the only PDF engine; MuPDF and its guardrail debt are deleted; the Papers view geometry (fit, integer sizing, focal zoom, scroll policies, smooth zoom) is ported and oracle-tested; the real PpsView oracle and pinned reference submodule are in place; the engine-seam import boundary is enforced; docs/PDF.md, CONTEXT.md, and the ADRs are updated. Shipped across PRs #118-#132. Follow-ups filed for page rotation, the PERF-2 re-baseline, and the EPUB bench measurement.

title: Make TuxBooks consume the fork's build output
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-vpt

## What to build

Choose how the fork's WASM and JS artifacts are produced, then make TuxBooks run them end to end. Evaluate a local emscripten build (emsdk 4.0.8, `platform/wasm`), a fork that commits prebuilt `dist/`, and a deterministic TuxBooks build step against the spec's criteria, and record the choice with the exact build command. Then make the frontend resolve the `mupdf` package to the fork so the app opens a real PDF and rasterizes pages using fork artifacts, with exactly one `mupdf` in the install. - [ ] Artifact-production mechanism chosen and recorded with rationale and the exact build command

- [ ] A seeded PDF opens, the first page renders, and scroll and zoom work in the built app
- [ ] The WASM asset plugin resolves from the package root and fails the build when outside `vendor/`
- [ ] Range-backed open, worker, `Module.locateFile`, cancellation, and caching are unchanged
- [ ] Fork build artifacts are not duplicated into the TuxBooks source tree

title: Integrate the TuxBooks MuPDF.js fork as a Git submodule
description:
## Problem Statement

The MuPDF.js implementation TuxBooks actually renders with is an opaque
registry install (`mupdf@1.28.1` in the frontend's dependency tree). When a
PDF rendering bug lives inside MuPDF.js itself, developers and AI coding
agents have no source to read, no seams to debug, and no way to patch the
engine and have TuxBooks run the patch. Every PDF fix that belongs in the
engine is currently blocked behind an opaque `node_modules` package.

## Solution

Maintain a TuxBooks fork of MuPDF.js and make it the engine TuxBooks runs.
The fork is added to the repo as a Git submodule at `vendor/mupdf`, pinned
to the `tuxbooks` branch, so the full source is present locally and can be
inspected and modified alongside TuxBooks. The frontend consumes the fork's
build output, so the running app executes fork artifacts rather than the
registry package, while the existing PDF engine boundary and range-backed
worker architecture stay exactly as they are. Provenance is proven twice: a
build-time guard that fails when the engine is not the fork, and a runtime
attribute asserted by the seeded PDF end-to-end suite.

This spec covers **Phase A (integration) only**. Editing MuPDF.js source is
Phase B and does not start automatically.

## User Stories

1.  As an AI coding agent, I want the complete MuPDF.js source in the
    repository, so that I can read the real rendering implementation instead
    of an opaque package.
2.  As an AI coding agent, I want to modify MuPDF.js source locally, so that
    I can fix PDF bugs at their source rather than working around them.
3.  As a developer, I want the exact upstream MuPDF version and commit
    recorded, so that I can judge how far the fork has diverged.
4.  As a maintainer, I want the fork pinned by a submodule commit, so that a
    build is reproducible and an engine change is an explicit pointer bump.
5.  As a maintainer, I want TuxBooks to actually execute the fork, so that
    fork changes reach users.
6.  As a maintainer, I want one unambiguous MuPDF dependency, so that edits
    to the fork cannot be silently ignored in favour of a registry copy.
7.  As a CI system, I want a guard that fails when the resolved engine is not
    the fork, so that a regression to the registry package is caught.
8.  As a user, I want PDF opening, first-page rendering, scrolling, zoom,
    search, and outline to keep working, so that the integration has no
    behavioural cost.
9.  As a developer, I want the range-backed open path preserved, so that
    large PDFs never load wholly into memory.
10. As a developer, I want worker isolation and the `Module.locateFile`
    wiring preserved, so that rasterization stays off the UI thread.
11. As a developer, I want the PDF engine seam preserved, so that MuPDF
    imports never leak into React components.
12. As a fresh contributor, I want a submodule-including clone to give a
    working tree, so that setup is one command.
13. As a fresh contributor, I want documented build and update commands, so
    that I can build the fork and bump it without re-deriving the procedure.
14. As a maintainer, I want TuxBooks-specific engine changes committed on the
    `tuxbooks` branch of the fork, so that they are reviewable separately.
15. As a maintainer, I want TuxBooks to record the exact fork commit, so that
    an engine change is visible in the repo history.
16. As an agent, I want generated artifacts, toolchains, caches, and
    `node_modules` excluded from commits, so that both repositories' history
    stays clean.
17. As a security reviewer, I want the dual-install risk assessed and
    documented, so that our supply-chain expectations are explicit.
18. As a developer, I want the WASM asset seam to resolve from the installed
    package root, so that it follows whichever MuPDF package is installed.
19. As the E2E suite, I want a runtime provenance attribute, so that I can
    assert the running app loaded the fork's WASM.
20. As a maintainer, I want the emitted WASM inspected against the fork's
    build, so that a stale artifact cannot masquerade as the fork.
21. As a maintainer, I want Phase A to stop before source changes, so that
    integration failures and engine bugs are separable.
22. As a maintainer, I want a Phase A report, so that I know how to build,
    update, and debug the fork before Phase B begins.
23. As a release process, I want the fork's build requirements captured, so
    that packaging does not depend on an undeclared toolchain.
24. As a maintainer, I want existing docs updated instead of duplicated, so
    that there is one source of truth.
25. As a maintainer, I want fresh-clone verification, so that the submodule
    story is proven rather than assumed.
26. As a developer, I want a documented check that no registry `mupdf`
    remains, so that accidental dual installs are detectable.
27. As a maintainer, I want the supply-chain gate's treatment of the local
    dependency explicit, so that bypassing the maturity floor is deliberate.
28. As a user, I want the fork's WASM to be what rasterizes my PDFs, so that
    TuxBooks-specific engine fixes actually reach me.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Submodule, not vendoring.** `vendor/mupdf` is registered as a Git
  submodule tracking the fork's `tuxbooks` branch. The fork's files are never
  copied into the TuxBooks tree, and upstream history is never rewritten.
- **Fork identity.** Repository `tuxbooks/mupdf`, a fork of the main MuPDF
  repository `ArtifexSoftware/mupdf`. The `tuxbooks` branch is created from
  upstream tag `1.28.1`, matching the installed `mupdf` dependency. The
  MuPDF.js/WASM source and build live at `platform/wasm/`; the separate
  `ArtifexSoftware/mupdf.js` repository stopped carrying the build on
  2025-05-27 and is docs and examples only.
- **Artifact production is decided in the consume ticket, not guessed.** How
  the fork's WASM and JS artifacts are produced and consumed (a local
  emscripten build, a fork that commits prebuilt `dist/`, or a deterministic
  TuxBooks build step) is resolved there against these criteria:
  - it produces the same artifacts the published `mupdf` package ships
    (JS API entry, type declarations, WASM binary and glue);
  - it keeps the package name `mupdf`, so the engine worker's import and the
    engine's types are unchanged;
  - it does not duplicate generated WASM/JS artifacts into the TuxBooks
    source tree;
  - it is deterministic and buildable from a clean checkout.
  Preferred shape: build the fork and consume it as a local package
  (workspace or file dependency). Fallback shape: a deterministic TuxBooks
  build step that builds the fork, produces published-equivalent artifacts,
  and makes them the runtime dependency.
- **Engine seam unchanged.** Only the PDF engine modules touch the engine.
  React components continue to import the main-thread engine seam only; the
  worker continues to own all engine objects and rasterization
  (ADR-0001's worker boundary is untouched).
- **WASM asset seam follows the package.** The Vite plugin that emits the
  WASM asset resolves it from the resolved package root instead of a
  hardcoded registry path, and fails the build when the resolved location is
  not under `vendor/mupdf`. The virtual-module contract and the
  `Module.locateFile` handoff are unchanged.
- **Non-regression contract.** The following must keep working: range-backed
  PDF opening through the `tuxbooks://` protocol; worker-based rendering;
  WASM worker isolation; `Module.locateFile`; render cancellation; document
  lifetime management; PDF virtualization; bitmap caching; first-page fast
  rendering.
- **Provenance.** A build-time constant carrying fork identity (repository,
  branch, commit) is exposed as a reader attribute and asserted in the seeded
  PDF E2E, so the running app proves which engine it loaded.
- **Supply chain.** A local/file/workspace dependency bypasses the registry
  integrity hash and the 30-day maturity floor; the decision ticket records
  this as a deliberate, documented carve-out, and verifies the lockfile and
  install no longer resolve the registry `mupdf` when the fork is the
  runtime.
- **Documentation.** The fork's purpose, upstream/fork/branch, update
  procedure, build procedure, consumption path, and the split between
  MuPDF.js changes and TuxBooks integration changes are documented in the
  existing PDF and build docs, or in one new doc referenced from them. No
  duplicate documents.
- **Commit discipline.** Generated build directories, downloaded toolchains,
  temporary WASM products, `node_modules`, caches, and local test artifacts
  are not committed unless the fork explicitly tracks a generated artifact.
  Both `.gitignore` files are respected.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test here asserts external behaviour and provenance: which engine
  the built app resolves and runs, and that the reader still behaves. It does
  not assert internal call shapes or module wiring.
- **Seam 1, provenance guard (offline, part of `just check`).** Asserts that
  the resolved `mupdf` realpath is under `vendor/mupdf`, that no registry
  copy survives anywhere in the install, and that the emitted WASM matches
  the fork's build output. This is the primary "TuxBooks executes the fork"
  proof. Precedent: the offline supply-chain gate script.
- **Seam 2, runtime provenance attribute.** The seeded PDF E2E asserts the
  reader reports the fork's identity, so the proof holds for the artifact
  that actually ran, not just the install graph. Precedent: the existing
  `data-pdf-*` reader attributes.
- **Seam 3, behavioural no-regression.** The existing seeded PDF E2E suites
  (reader open, first page, scroll, zoom, search, outline, worker source
  fetchable) run unchanged. Precedent: `engine-smoke` and `pdf-reader`
  suites.
- **Fresh-clone verification** is documented manual verification (networked,
  not a CI gate): clone with submodules, confirm the submodule is populated
  on the `tuxbooks` branch, follow the documented build, and open a PDF.
- **Full gate** is `just check`, plus the PDF E2E phases, before the
  integration is called complete.

## Out of Scope

- Phase B: any modification to MuPDF.js source. This spec ends with a report
  and a stop.
- Redesigning the PDF reader, its virtualization, caching, zoom, text layer,
  Smart Dark, or open telemetry.
- Replacing the PDFium import-time cover path.
- Windows or macOS packaging.
- Publishing the fork to a registry, or changing upstream.

## Further Notes

- **Current integration points** (anchors for the implementation): the
  frontend package's `mupdf` dependency; the WASM plugin in the Vite config
  and its `virtual:mupdf-wasm-url` module; the engine worker's dynamic
  `import("mupdf")`; the engine seam; the rendering and opening sections of
  the PDF doc; the build doc; the supply-chain doc. These confirm the single
  import surface and the hardcoded registry path that must be replaced.
- **Phase A report.** When integration works, report: (1) exact MuPDF.js
  version/commit; (2) exact upstream MuPDF version/commit; (3) how the WASM
  artifact is produced; (4) how TuxBooks consumes it; (5) the important
  MuPDF.js extension points; (6) limitations discovered; (7) exact command to
  build the fork; (8) exact command to update the fork in TuxBooks. Then stop
  and wait for the first engine bug/fix task.
- **Update workflow to document:** fetch and fast-forward the fork branch,
  commit changes on `tuxbooks`, push, then stage the submodule pointer
  change in TuxBooks with a clear message.
- **Worktree rule:** work happens on a branch in a fresh worktree under
  `.worktrees/`, never on `main`.

title: Settings cleanup and General rebuild
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-9qi

## What to build

Remove the Advanced tab entirely: drop `"advanced"` from the settings section union, from the `SECTIONS` list, and from `SECTION_ROWS`, delete the test that clicks it, and regenerate the `graft` snapshots for the changed files.

title: Hints on the contents drawer tabs
description:
## Parent

tuxbooks-9qi

## What to build

Give every contents drawer tab a hint. Wrap each tab trigger (`Pages`, `Outline`, `Bookmarks`, `Highlights`, `Search`, and EPUB `Contents`) in a Radix tooltip that shows a one-line description on hover and focus, with the shortcut appended where the tab has one. Add `aria-keyshortcuts` to the tabs that have a key.

Copy, exactly:
- Pages: "Thumbnails of every page, click one to jump there. (Ctrl+Shift+C)"
- Outline: "The document's own headings, in order."
- Bookmarks: "Pages you saved, so you can return to them. (Ctrl+Shift+B)"
- Highlights: "Text you highlighted, with any notes you added. (Ctrl+Shift+H)"
- Search: "Find text in this book. (Ctrl+F)"
- Contents (EPUB): "The book's chapters, in order. (Ctrl+Shift+C)"

The shortcut string comes from the `readerShortcuts` module, not typed next to the sentence. `TooltipProvider` already wraps the app, so no new provider is needed. Do not add a persistent hint line, do not wire the tooltip as `aria-describedby`, and leave the empty states and the header Contents button as they are.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the six tabs shows a tooltip on hover and on focus.
- [ ] The tooltip copy matches the list above.
- [ ] Pages, EPUB Contents, Bookmarks, Highlights, and Search show their shortcut; Outline shows none.
- [ ] Tabs with a key carry `aria-keyshortcuts` (Control on non-macOS, Meta on macOS).
- [ ] The visible tab label remains the accessible name; no `aria-describedby` is added.
- [ ] Empty states and the header Contents button are unchanged.
- [ ] Reader-side tests cover the tooltip text and the `aria-keyshortcuts` attribute.

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately).

title: Reader drawer tab hints and Settings cleanup
description:
## Problem Statement

Two rough edges in the reader and Settings.

The contents drawer's tabs (Pages, Outline, Bookmarks, Highlights, Search, and EPUB Contents) are bare labels. Nothing on hover or focus explains what each panel holds, and nothing tells a keyboard user the shortcut that lands there. A reader has to click each tab to learn what it is.

Settings shows prose that is not a setting. The Advanced tab contains two static rows, "Storage: Local only" and "Full-text search: SQLite FTS5", the second of which is implementation detail. The PDF tab repeats two more static rows, "Rendering" and "Outlines and thumbnails", that describe the renderer rather than a preference. The General tab's three rows describe actions that live in the header and sidebar (import, collections) instead of offering them. The result is a Settings surface that reads like documentation and buries the one real control on each page.

## Solution

Add a tooltip to every contents drawer tab, with a one-line description and the shortcut where one exists, and expose the shortcut to assistive tech with `aria-keyshortcuts`. Remove the static, non-setting rows and the Advanced tab. Rebuild General around real controls: keep the app theme, and add a Library block with "Add library folder…" and "Import books…" that run the same pickers the header uses.

## User Stories

1. As a reader, I want a hint on the Pages tab, so that I know it is a thumbnail grid before I click it.
2. As a reader, I want a hint on the Outline tab, so that I know it is the document's own headings.
3. As a reader, I want a hint on the Bookmarks tab, so that I know it lists pages I saved.
4. As a reader, I want a hint on the Highlights tab, so that I know it lists my highlights and notes.
5. As a reader, I want a hint on the Search tab, so that I know it searches this book.
6. As an EPUB reader, I want a hint on the Contents tab, so that I know it is the chapter list.
7. As a reader, I want each tab hint to show its shortcut where one exists, so that I learn the key while using the mouse.
8. As a keyboard user, I want the tab shortcut on the tab itself, so that focus reveals the same information as hover.
9. As a screen reader user, I want the tab shortcut announced, so that I know a key exists.
10. As a reader, I do not want a persistent hint line taking space in the tray, so that the panel stays compact.
11. As a reader, I do not want hints on empty states, so that the panel does not explain nothing.
12. As a user, I want the Advanced tab gone, so that Settings contains settings rather than trivia.
13. As a PDF reader, I want the Rendering and Outlines rows gone from the PDF tab, so that the page shows only the appearance setting it controls.
14. As a reader, I want the Reading tab's "How defaults are saved" prose gone, so that all reader tabs are consistent.
15. As a user, I want General to keep the app theme control, so that the one app-wide preference stays where it is.
16. As a user, I want a way to add a library folder from Settings, so that I do not have to hunt in the header.
17. As a user, I want an Import books action in Settings, so that importing is reachable from where I look for settings.
18. As a user, I want a hint explaining that added folders become watched locations and that drag and drop also imports, so that the model is clear.
19. As a user, I want the Collections row gone from General, so that I am not told about a sidebar action I can already see.
20. As a maintainer, I want the removed sections' tests updated, so that the suite reflects the surface.
21. As a maintainer, I want the graft snapshots regenerated for the changed files, so that the graph does not go stale.
22. As a user, I want Data and Keyboard Shortcuts untouched, so that this cleanup does not disturb what already works.

## Implementation Decisions

- Drawer hints are Radix tooltips on each `TabsTrigger`, matching the header button tooltip idiom. `TooltipProvider` already wraps the app in `AppShell`, and the drawer portal preserves React context, so no new provider is needed.
- Hint content is one line per tab, with the shortcut appended in parentheses where the tab has one. The shortcut string comes from the `readerShortcuts` module so it cannot drift. Proposed copy:
  - Pages: "Thumbnails of every page, click one to jump there. (Ctrl+Shift+C)"
  - Outline: "The document's own headings, in order."
  - Bookmarks: "Pages you saved, so you can return to them. (Ctrl+Shift+B)"
  - Highlights: "Text you highlighted, with any notes you added. (Ctrl+Shift+H)"
  - Search: "Find text in this book. (Ctrl+F)"
  - Contents (EPUB): "The book's chapters, in order. (Ctrl+Shift+C)"
- Tabs with a key carry `aria-keyshortcuts`, set from the platform-aware formatter. The visible tab label stays the accessible name. Tooltip text is not wired as `aria-describedby`, to avoid reading every tab twice.
- Empty states and the header Contents button are untouched.
- Settings cleanup: remove the `advanced` section from the type union, the `SECTIONS` list, and `SECTION_ROWS`; delete its test; regenerate the graft snapshots for the touched files.
- PDF tab: remove the "Rendering" and "Outlines and thumbnails" rows from `SECTION_ROWS.pdf`; keep the "Default PDF appearance" card.
- Reading tab: remove the "How defaults are saved" row from `SECTION_ROWS.reading`.
- General tab: keep the App theme control and its hint. Replace the three static rows with a Library block using the existing `useImport()` and bridge pickers: "Add library folder…" calls `pickDirectory()` then `importPaths([dir])`; "Import books…" calls `pickBookFiles()` then `importPaths(files)`, both only when the picker returns something. Add a hint that added folders become watched library locations and that dragging files onto the window also imports.
- Data and Keyboard Shortcuts sections are unchanged.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests drive the UI as a user would and assert observable behavior: a tooltip's text on hover or focus, a tab's `aria-keyshortcuts`, a section's rendered rows, a button calling the picker and import. They do not assert component internals.
- Primary seams: the existing reader-side component tests for the drawer tabs (render the shell, open the drawer, hover or focus a tab, assert the tooltip text and `aria-keyshortcuts`), and the existing settings component test for the cleanup (assert Advanced is gone, General shows the two actions, PDF and Reading no longer show the removed strings).
- The General Library actions are tested through the settings seam with the bridge mocked: clicking "Add library folder…" resolves `pickDirectory` and calls `importPaths` with the folder; "Import books…" resolves `pickBookFiles` and calls `importPaths` with the files. Prior art is the existing settings tests that mock `mockInvoke` and the import tests.
- Update `frontend/tests/SettingsShell.test.tsx` for the removed sections and the new General controls.

In the PDF reader, mod+shift+T toggles the docked page-thumbnails sidebar, mod+shift+A toggles the appearance popover, and mod+shift+C toggles the contents drawer. title: Reader keyboard shortcuts for panels, plus a full Settings reference
description:
## Problem Statement

Keyboard access to the reader is uneven. Search has Ctrl/Cmd+F and bookmark has Ctrl/Cmd+B, and both say so in their tooltips, but page thumbnails, appearance, and the contents/bookmarks/highlights drawer have no shortcuts at all. A keyboard user can turn pages and search, then has to reach for the mouse to open a panel. The Settings "Keyboard Shortcuts" list makes it worse: it shows six rows and omits the drawer, thumbnails, appearance, zoom, fit modes, presentation, and library navigation, so the reference is both incomplete and quietly wrong.

## Solution

Give the three controls that lack keys a consistent shortcut, and add direct shortcuts for the drawer's Bookmarks and Highlights tabs. The scheme is mod+shift plus a mnemonic letter, the same family as the VS Code activity bar. Update the tooltips and add `aria-keyshortcuts` so the keys are discoverable. Replace the Settings shortcuts list with a complete reference, built from one source of truth and grouped by where each key works. Update the PDF and EPUB docs.

## User Stories

1. As a reader, I want a shortcut to open and close page thumbnails, so that I can browse pages without reaching for the mouse.
2. As a reader, I want a shortcut to open and close the appearance panel, so that I can change theme and text without a click.
3. As a reader, I want a shortcut to open and close the contents drawer, so that I can reach the outline and bookmarks from the keyboard.
4. As a reader, I want a shortcut to open the drawer straight to Bookmarks, so that I skip tabbing through other tabs.
5. As a reader, I want a shortcut to open the drawer straight to Highlights, so that I skip tabbing through other tabs.
6. As a reader, I want each drawer shortcut to close the drawer when it is already open, so that the key behaves as a toggle.
7. As a reader, I want a drawer shortcut pressed while the drawer is open to close it whatever tab is showing, so that the behavior is predictable.
8. As a reader, I want opening a panel to leave keyboard focus in the reader, so that arrows and space keep turning pages.
9. As a reader, I want the appearance key to close an open popover, and Escape to close it too, so that it behaves like the zoom menu.
10. As a reader in presentation mode, I want the drawer and thumbnail keys to keep working, so that full screen does not lose the panels.
11. As a reader of an EPUB, I want the drawer and appearance keys to work, so that the same keys work in both formats.
12. As a PDF reader, I want the thumbnail key to exist only where thumbnails exist, so that EPUB does not advertise a key that does nothing.
13. As a reader, I want the key shown in each tooltip, so that I learn it while using the mouse.
14. As a screen reader user, I want the shortcut announced on the button, so that I know a key exists before I press it.
15. As a screen reader user on macOS, I want the announced modifier to be Cmd, not Ctrl, so that the key I hear is the key I press.
16. As a reader, I want the Settings shortcuts reference to list everything, so that I can learn a key I did not know existed.
17. As a reader, I want the reference grouped by where the keys work, so that I can find the reader keys without scanning library keys.
18. As a reader, I want the reference to show only keys worth teaching, so that bare aliases and text-field keys do not drown it.
19. As a macOS reader, I want the reference to show Cmd rather than Ctrl, so that it matches my keyboard.
20. As a maintainer, I want the reference to come from one source of truth, so that it cannot drift from the registered shortcuts again.
21. As a maintainer, I want a test that the reference lists the new keys, so that a future edit cannot silently drop one.
22. As a maintainer, I want the shortcut data typed, so that an entry missing a scope or combo fails the type check.
23. As a reader, I want the PDF doc to list the reader shortcuts, so that I can find them outside the app.
24. As a reader of an EPUB, I want the EPUB doc to list the shared shortcuts, so that I know which apply to me.
25. As a reader, I do not want to remap shortcuts, so that the app stays simple and the defaults stay consistent.
26. As a reader, I do not want a shortcut for the library right-click menu, because it is not part of the PDF viewer.
27. As a reader, I want the new keys to avoid the keys already in use, so that nothing I know stops working.

## Implementation Decisions

- Scheme: mod+shift plus a mnemonic letter. `mod` resolves to Ctrl or Cmd through the existing engine.
- Keys: mod+shift+T page thumbnails, mod+shift+A appearance, mod+shift+C contents drawer, mod+shift+B bookmarks tab, mod+shift+H highlights tab.
- Conflict check: none of the five collide with the registered combos (mod+F, mod+B, mod+L, mod+K, mod+0 through mod+3, mod plus and minus, arrows, space, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, shift+space).
- Behavior: thumbnails and the drawer are true toggles. A tab key opens the drawer on that tab and the same key closes it. Any drawer shortcut closes the drawer when it is already open, regardless of tab. No shortcut moves focus into a panel. Appearance opens and closes the popover; Escape also closes it.
- Scope attaches to the control, not the format. Thumbnails are PDF-only, gated with the existing `isEpub ? null : ...` pattern. The drawer and appearance work in PDF and EPUB. Search stays mod+F, bookmark stays mod+B. Nothing registers in the library, because the shortcuts live in the reader shell and unmount with it.
- The shortcut reference is data-driven from one typed module that lists each action with its combos, scope, and display group. Settings renders from it. Registration stays where the controls live; the module is the single home for what the user sees.
- Tooltips show the key in the existing style (`Page thumbnails (Ctrl+Shift+T)`), keeping the Ctrl wording the current tooltips already use.
- `aria-keyshortcuts` is set on each button from a platform-aware helper: `Meta+Shift+T` on macOS, `Control+Shift+T` elsewhere.
- Settings representation: the existing `shortcuts` section keeps its id and title and becomes a grouped two-column reference. Groups in order: Global, Library, Reader, PDF reader. Keys render in a `kbd` style. The modifier display is platform-aware, Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere.
- Reference contents. Global: focus search (mod+K), close dialog or overlay (Esc). Library: move selection (arrows), first or last book (Home/End), open selected book (Enter). Reader, both formats: next page or section (Right, Space, PageDown), previous (Left, PageUp), first or last (Home/End), search (mod+F), bookmark (mod+B), presentation (mod+L), leave presentation (Esc). PDF reader extras: thumbnails (mod+shift+T), appearance (mod+shift+A), contents (mod+shift+C), bookmarks tab (mod+shift+B), highlights tab (mod+shift+H), zoom in (mod+Plus), zoom out (mod+Minus), reset zoom (mod+0), fit page/width/auto (mod+1, mod+2, mod+3), reverse page flip in presentation (Shift+Space).
- Reference omissions: the bare `+`, `=`, and `-` zoom aliases; the EPUB engine-owned navigation keys, already listed under Reader; the Enter and Escape keys inside the page and zoom fields; and the dev-only F12 and Ctrl+Shift+I.
- Shortcuts stay fixed. No remapping, no capture UI, no settings store.
- Docs: `docs/PDF.md` and `docs/EPUB.md` each get a shortcuts block, with EPUB noting which keys apply to it.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests drive keys through the window the way a user would (`fireEvent.keyDown(window, ...)`) and assert the observable UI: a panel opened or closed, the active tab, the rendered reference rows. They do not assert registration internals.
- Primary seam: the existing reader-shell component test. It renders the shell with a mocked book format and already covers reader shortcuts, so the toggle and tab behavior lands there for both PDF and EPUB.
- Settings seam: the existing settings component test. It already opens the Keyboard Shortcuts section, so the grouped reference and its rows are asserted there.
- Unit seam: a new test for the shortcut data module, asserting each group and that the new keys are present with the right scope.
- Prior art: the reader-shell shortcut blocks (presentation, navigation, bookmark), the `comboFromEvent` shift case in the shortcuts test (mod+shift already parses), and the settings section test.
- One end-to-end check is not required; the component seam covers the behavior. If added later, it types a drawer key and asserts the panel.

## Out of Scope

- Remappable shortcuts.
- The library right-click menu and its collection submenus.
- EPUB-only shortcuts beyond what the shared reader already provides.
- A global "?" cheat-sheet overlay.
- Changing the existing tooltip wording on platforms other than what is described.

## Further Notes

- The appearance panel is a transient popover today, not a docked surface. Its shortcut treats it as a toggle.
- If a future key needs to move, it moves in code. The data module makes the Settings copy follow.
- The existing Settings list is the reason for the one-source-of-truth decision: it drifted into being wrong.

title: Add typed page-number entry to the PDF page controls
description:
## Problem Statement

A reader working through a long PDF can only change pages with the prev/next buttons, a thumbnail click, the navigation drawer page grid, or scrolling. The "Page X of Y" readout looks like a field but is plain text, so there is no way to type a page number and jump straight to it. Reaching a known page in a 900 page document means clicking next hundreds of times or hunting in the sidebar.

## Solution

The page readout in the PDF header toolbar and in the presentation bar becomes an editable page field. A reader clicks or tabs into it, types a page number, and presses Enter to jump. The wheel steps pages while the field is focused, and the Up/Down arrows step one page. Invalid entries revert, out-of-range entries clamp, and Escape restores the current page. The behavior matches the zoom field beside it, so the toolbar has one consistent input idiom.

## User Stories

1. As a reader, I want to click the page number in the toolbar, so that I can type a target page.
2. As a reader, I want clicking the field to select the whole current value, so that typing replaces it instead of appending.
3. As a reader, I want to type a page number and press Enter, so that the reader jumps to that page.
4. As a reader, I want leaving the field with the mouse to commit a changed value, so that I do not have to press Enter.
5. As a reader, I want Escape to abandon my edit and keep the current page, so that a mistaken edit is easy to undo.
6. As a reader, I want an empty or non-numeric entry to leave the page unchanged, so that a slip costs nothing.
7. As a reader, I want a number past the last page to jump to the last page, so that I land somewhere sensible.
8. As a reader, I want a number below one to jump to the first page, so that I land somewhere sensible.
9. As a reader, I want Up and Down arrows to step one page while the field is focused, so that I can nudge the page without leaving the field.
10. As a reader, I want the wheel over the focused field to step one page per tick, so that I can turn pages with the mouse.
11. As a reader, I want the wheel over an unfocused field to do nothing, so that a pointer gliding over the toolbar does not turn the page behind my back.
12. As a reader, I want the wheel to ignore ticks with Ctrl, Meta, or Alt held, so that modified wheels stay with zoom.
13. As a reader, I want the prev and next buttons to keep working exactly as before, so that my old habit still works.
14. As a reader, I want the field disabled until the document has loaded, so that I cannot type a page into a document that has no pages yet.
15. As a reader in presentation mode, I want the same editable field on the floating bar, so that a full-screen reading session can still jump to a page.
16. As a reader, I want typing a page and clicking a thumbnail to land the target page in the same place, so that the jump is predictable.
17. As a reader, I want the field width to fit the page count, so that the toolbar does not jump around as I flip pages.
18. As a reader, I want to see the total page count next to the field, so that I know the range I can jump into.
19. As a reader, I want the total page count to stay read-only, so that I cannot type a nonsense range.
20. As a reader, I want the page number to persist like any other page change, so that reopening the book returns me to it.
21. As a keyboard-only reader, I want to reach the field with Tab, so that I can change pages without a mouse.
22. As a screen reader user, I want the new page announced after a jump, so that I know where I landed.
23. As a screen reader user, I do not want every keystroke announced, so that typing a number is not noisy.
24. As a touch or on-screen keyboard user, I want a numeric keyboard for the field, so that entry is quick.
25. As a reader, I want no spinner arrows inside the field, so that the toolbar stays compact and the arrows mean something else.
26. As a reader, I want the field to show the live page as I scroll, so that it always reflects where I am.
27. As a reader, I want the jump to land the target page at the top of the viewport, matching every other navigation path.
28. As a reader, I want a mistyped multi-digit number to still land on a real page rather than erroring, so that the tool never blocks me.
29. As a reader, I want the same field styling as the zoom input, so that the toolbar looks coherent.
30. As a reader, I want the field to work in the docked shell header and in the standalone reader fallback, so that it works in every layout.

## Implementation Decisions

- The static page readout in the PDF header toolbar and in the presentation bar becomes an editable field. Both call sites share one component so the behavior cannot drift. The shared component lives in the PDF reader area; the zoom control stays separate because its percent and fit-popover behavior is a different concern.
- The field is controlled by a draft string, mirroring the zoom control: focus captures the current value and selects it, Enter and blur commit, Escape clears the draft and restores the live page.
- A page-parse helper sits with the existing page math (the module that owns `positionToPage` and `pageToPosition`). It returns a clamped integer for a numeric entry, and null for empty or non-numeric input. This parallels the existing zoom percent parse and the progress parser, which already validates integer page bounds.
- Commit routes through the existing `goToPage` path, which clamps to `[1, pageCount]`. A typed jump therefore uses the same page-change and scroll machinery as thumbnails, the drawer, the outline, and restore. No new scroll logic is introduced.
- The wheel listener is attached natively with `{ passive: false }` and calls `preventDefault`, because React registers wheel handlers passively and a `preventDefault` inside `onWheel` does nothing. It steps one page per tick above a small delta threshold, ignores ticks with Ctrl, Meta, or Alt held, and only acts while the field has focus. This mirrors the existing Ctrl+wheel zoom listener.
- Up and Down arrow keys step one page while the field is focused.
- The field is disabled until the layout is ready, which is the same condition that gates the rest of the page controls.
- The field width is derived from the digit count of the page count so the toolbar does not shift.
- The input uses `inputMode="numeric"` and `autocomplete="off"`, and renders no native spin buttons.
- Accessibility: the existing wrapper keeps the `pdf-page-indicator` identity and holds a visually hidden live region that announces "Page X of Y" after a jump. The editable input carries its own test identity. `aria-live` is not placed on the input.
- The total page count stays read-only text beside the field.
- No global keyboard shortcut is added. A go-to-page chord such as `mod+g` collides with the browser expectation of find-next and with the existing `mod+f` search, so Tab plus the visible field covers the keyboard path instead.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests drive the field with user events and assert observable outcomes: the input value, the rendered canvas page, and scroll-into-view calls. They do not assert internal state or implementation shape.
- The primary seam is the existing PDF reader component test suite, which renders the reader with a mocked pdfium document inside the reader provider. It already owns navigation, controls docking, scroll tracking, zoom anchoring, and presentation coverage, so the new behavior lands there.
- The wheel, arrow stepping, commit, revert, clamp, disabled-until-ready, and landing behavior are covered at that seam. The presentation bar field is covered at the same seam through the presentation tests.
- Prior art: the existing navigation and controls-docking blocks, the zoom field commit and revert tests, and the shortcut tests.
- One end-to-end smoke in the PDF reader spec types a page number and asserts the canvas page, exercising the real DOM path. Existing selectors that read the page indicator are updated to the new field identity.

## Out of Scope

- EPUB navigation. It is section-based and has no page numbers.
- The navigation drawer page grid stays click-only.
- No go-to-page dialog or popover; the field is inline and always present.
- The zoom percent field is unchanged.
- No shortcut to focus the field.
- No change to how the page count is computed or displayed.
- No typed navigation for any unit other than a page number.

## Further Notes

- The wheel is scoped to focus on purpose. Hover stepping would turn pages whenever the pointer crossed the toolbar mid-scroll, which reads as a bug.
- Silent clamping has one honest rough edge: a fat-fingered 500 instead of 50 lands at the end of the book. Every mainstream viewer accepts this, and an error state costs more than it fixes.
- The design follows the page fields in Chrome, Firefox, Acrobat, Okular, and Preview, so most readers need no instruction.
